root_cause.text: In rds_message_purge(), the zerocopy send cleanup path incorrectly used rm->m_rs (socket association) as the indicator for zerocopy state instead of checking the presence of op_mmp_znotifier, causing a failure to properly clean up pinned pages and release the znotifier when a zerocopy send fails before the message is queued on the socket.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the old code only handled the zerocopy notifier inside the `if (rm->m_rs)` block, while the fix captures `op_mmp_znotifier` upfront and adds a separate `else if (znotifier)` branch to handle the unqueued case by calling `mm_unaccount_pinned_pages()` and freeing the notifier. The CVE description confirms that "the purge path currently infers zerocopy state from rm->m_rs, so an unqueued message can be cleaned up as if it owned normal payload pages."

candidates.rationale: This condition incorrectly uses rm->m_rs as the indicator for zerocopy state. When a zerocopy send fails before the message is queued on the socket, rm->m_rs may be NULL, causing the entire zerocopy cleanup block to be skipped, thereby failing to release the znotifier and unpin pages.

This statement extracts the socket association from the message. It is executed only when rm->m_rs is non-NULL; the vulnerability stems from the fact that this assignment and subsequent cleanup are not reached when rm->m_rs is NULL but a znotifier exists.

This check for the zerocopy notifier is only reached if the outer condition rm->m_rs is true. The vulnerability is that this check should be performed independently of rm->m_rs, because a znotifier may exist even when ro->m_rs is NULL.

This function call performs the actual cleanup of pinned pages and the zerocopy notifier. It is only executed inside the outer if block; when rm->m_rs is NULL, this cleanup is missed, leaving resources leaked.

This statement clears the zerocopy notifier pointer. It is also only reached when rm->m_rs is non-NULL, so if the outer condition fails, the notifier is never cleared, leading to potential use-after-free or double-free.

bic_trace_step.reason: In rds_message_purge(), the zerocopy cleanup path (lines 85-94 in the diff) only invokes rds_rm_zerocopy_callback and sets zcopy=true if rm->m_rs is non-NULL. This incorrectly uses the socket association as the indicator for zerocopy state, instead of checking the presence of op_mmp_znotifier alone. Consequently, if a message has a znotifier but rm->m_rs is NULL (e.g., when a zerocopy send fails before queuing on the socket), the znotifier is leaked and pinned pages are freed with __free_page instead of put_page, leaving the vulnerability described.
